lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write two sentences that acknowledge a source and promise not to invent details.

FEEDBACK
Acknowledgement names the approved text/source; promise avoids invented sacred content.

CHECK
Changing a cultural story "to make it funnier" can be disrespectful and inaccurate.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
From an approved classroom or published children's source only, write a short respectful retell (100–120 words) with a source line. Add a note listing one detail you refused to invent.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Retelling with respect means using approved sources, keeping important meanings accurate and acknowledging where the story came from.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: From an approved classroom or published children's source only, write a short respectful retell (100–120 words) with a source line. Add a note listing one detail you refused to invent. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original demonstration: "This retell follows our class text from [source named in materials]. I kept the order of events and did not add new sacred details." Acknowledgement plus accuracy.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Changing a cultural story "to make it funnier" can be disrespectful and inaccurate. Correction: Acknowledgement names the approved text/source; promise avoids invented sacred content.

Parent: Likely misconception: Changing a cultural story "to make it funnier" can be disrespectful and inaccurate. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

teach_steps.explain:
Retelling with respect means using approved sources, keeping important meanings accurate and acknowledging where the story came from.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
